content: Context: [Skewing the stator slots by one slot pitch reduces cogging torque by up to 15% while maintaining 98% of the rated torque output.] Question: How does skewing affect cogging torque?

According to the documents, skewing the stator slots by one slot pitch reduces cogging torque by up to 15% with only a 2% loss in rated torque output. This is a common technique because it distributes the reluctance variation more evenly around the rotor, smoothing out torque ripple.

I do not have enough information in the provided documents to answer this, but based on general knowledge: end-of-life NdFeB magnets from electric motors are typically recycled through hydrometallurgical or pyrometallurgical processes to recover rare earth elements such as neodymium and dysprosium, which are then reused in new magnet production.
